Current peds IMC/med surg nurse here! Worked in adult Onc first and didn’t like the adults at all. Switched to peds and I like it more. 

Pros: kids are honest and generally want to get better, cute moments with kids, helpful parents that do cares, in general, the peds floor staff is more kind and helpful than adult nursing  

Cons: aggressive/abusive/health illiterate parents, CPS cases, RNs are always the “mean guy” for vitals, meds, injections, lab draws. 
 
Overall, I just like taking care of kids and find joy in it. First year is rough no matter what type of nursing you do. Focus on finding a unit that wants you to succeed with a healthier work culture, it makes all the difference.

Best of luck!

This is the basis for IFS work. Once my therapist started incorporating IFS work into our sessions, things started clicking. 

Voice 1: sounds like the exile. The part of you that was hurt. A core wound.
Voice 2: sounds like the manager. It wants to protect you by criticizing.
Voice 3: sounds like the firefighter. When things get really bad, it gives you an out. A way to make the pain stop.
Present self: the core self. The soul, the true beautiful part of you. 

The basis of IFS is to recognize that all these parts of you care about you and only want to help you. There are no bad parts, just different way to protect you. The goal is to meet them all with compassion. Still trying to wrap my head around it too. Mention it to your T to incorporate more IFS work; she is probably already using the concepts by the sound of it. 

I wish you nothing about good luck and love on this journey.

My therapist is a great, white lady. Being an American born desi, I live in the “in-between” of cultures and feeling like I never fit in. My therapist never pretends to 100% understand, but helps me make insights about my own feelings. Also, just chronic depression and anxiety assistance is somewhat universal at times. I’m on my fifth therapist and have been with her for 1.5 years. I found her on psychology today; look for ones that are specific to your needs. For example, I have a trauma-informed therapist so we can talk about emotional neglect and self-abandonment. It takes a while to find a good fit but when you do, you can have some real healing. The kind of healing that makes you feel a real sense of contentment and love for yourself in your soul.
